ctx.x: Well, this was still just, what, a year after you'd gotten out of high school, right?

Yeah. So then I left there and went to Central Avenue and started to work for Curtis Moseby at the Apex Club? (WILLARD: The Apex Club?) (SIMMONS: no, what was the name of the club? Nemo.) (WILLARD: The Nemo Lounge.) Yeah. Well, now, Curtis Moseby was a bandleader. Curtis Moseby and his Blues Blowers.

items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: WILARD: You'd go to jail there? SIMMONS: AN SO -- yeah, yeah, they called it the slaughter house, then.

ctx.x: Well, they didn't want us to stop in Indio, it was a little small place, you know. He wanted us to keep on going, you know. So my friend and I, we rode the timbers. We didn't want to get locked up. 'Cause the train's first stop was at Lincoln Heights, you know? And we wanted to get off the train before Lincoln Heights. WILARD: You'd go to jail there? SIMMONS: AN SO -- yeah, yeah, they called it the slaughter house, then. Because it was about to shake down. Every time a train would pass, a crack would appear in…

Well, anyway, got ready to get off at Lincoln Park, and this big, big Mexican -- he must have weighed about 300 pounds -- well, now, you know when you get a light from a moving object, you try to find out how fast it's going so that you can get off with some kind of speed to keep from killing yourself, you know.
